android_mechanism: History persisted eagerly on every change; fix defers the save
bug_description: The search-history HistoryStore calls preferences flush() synchronously on every setItem/delItem (i.e., on every recorded search keyword), forcing a disk write on the caller's thread each time. Rapid successive searches each pay a full synchronous flush, adding avoidable I/O latency to the search flow.
fix_summary: Flushes are debounced: mutations update the in-memory cache synchronously and a single flush runs 2 seconds after the last mutation.

test_oracle.definition: raw-instruction-retired sample count attributed to the app process during the measured step, aggregated from perf.data (HapRay perf.db instruction counts).
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed over >= 3 rounds per variant

evidence.note: 3.29G vs 166M instructions (20x); cpu 6867 vs 328 ms; 1000 vs 1 flushes

mechanism_oracle.definition: Number of preference flush (fsync/disk write) operations attributable to the history store during a 10-search burst, and their total wall/CPU time from the disk trace.
mechanism_oracle.comparison: unfixed: 10 flushes (one per search) on the calling thread; fixed: 1 flush after the burst. unfixed disk-sync time on the search path > fixed by >= 5x for the burst.

reproduction: git -C hosts/interviewapp checkout case/interviewapp_search_history_sync_flush/unfixed; apply the measurement harness patch for this case, build, sign and install the HAP.
git -C hosts/interviewapp checkout case/interviewapp_search_history_sync_flush/fixed; rebuild, reinstall and repeat identically.
Compare test_oracle.metric across the two report sets: unfixed >= 1.2 * fixed.
